entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Poltava was a pivotal event in the Great Northern War, fought between the Tsardom of Russia and the Swedish Empire on July 8, 1709. This decisive battle took place in Poltava, Ukraine, and saw the Russian army, led by Peter the Great, emerge victorious against the Swedish forces under Charles XII. The outcome of the battle marked a significant turning point in the war, as it allowed Russia to gain control of the Azov region and ultimately led to the decline of the Swedish Empire.

The Battle of Poltava was a masterclass in military strategy and tactics, with the Russian army employing a novel combination of artillery and infantry tactics to outmaneuver the Swedish forces. The battle also saw the introduction of new military technologies, including the use of cannons and mortars, which would go on to play a crucial role in future conflicts.

The legacy of the Battle of Poltava can be seen in the rise of the Russian Empire, which would go on to become a dominant world power in the centuries to come. The battle also had a profound impact on the balance of power in Europe, as it marked the beginning of the end of Swedish dominance in the region.

The Battle of Poltava remains one of the most studied and revered battles in military history, with its tactics and strategies continuing to influence military leaders to this day.
